name: Wyoming

sales.rateNote: Statewide 4% sales and use tax (a 3% base plus 1% added on July 1, 1993, W.S. 39-15-104). Counties may add voter-approved 'pennies'; combined rates generally run from 4% to 8%. About 69% of the 4% goes to the state and 30% back to local governments.

local.levies: counties (general purpose up to 2%, specific purpose up to 2%, economic development up to 1%), cities and towns (up to 1%), and resort districts (up to 3%), all subject to voter approval
local.capNote: County general purpose, specific purpose and economic development taxes together may not exceed 3% (W.S. 39-15-204(a)(iv)); resort districts may levy up to 3% and cities up to 1% under separate paragraphs.

groceries.note: Food for domestic home consumption is exempt; restaurant (prepared) food, alcohol and tobacco are taxable. Local taxes follow the same exemptions (W.S. 39-15-205).

otherRates.note: Mandatory 5% statewide lodging tax (3% to the state, 2% to the local jurisdiction), plus optional local lodging tax up to 2% and sales tax.

sales.holidayNote: Wyoming has no sales tax holiday.

useTax.note: Use tax at the same rate as the sales tax of the jurisdiction (state 4% plus local), self-reported on goods bought outside Wyoming for use in the state.

facts.text: Wyoming's sales tax is destination-based: the rate is that of the county where the customer takes possession, generally between 4% and 8%.
Each local 'penny' must be approved by county voters; a defeated proposal cannot return to the ballot for at least 11 months.
Over-the-counter drugs are taxable; only prescribed drugs, insulin, oxygen and medical devices sold under prescription are exempt.
Refunds of sales tax paid in error must be requested from the vendor, not the Department of Revenue, within three years.
Resort districts can levy up to 3% of their own for general revenue.

property.levied: local (counties, school districts, cities and special districts), billed and collected by the county treasurer

assessment.text: Residential and most other property is assessed at 9.5% of fair market value (industrial property 11.5%). The assessed value of a single family home and its land may not rise more than 4% a year over the prior year (the excess is exempt), unless the owner bought it the prior year or made structural changes.
assessment.capText: Residential and most other property is assessed at 9.5% of fair market value (industrial property 11.5%). The assessed value of a single family home and its land may not rise more than 4% a year over the prior year (the excess is exempt), unless the owner bought it the prior year or made structural changes.

homestead.name: Homeowner tax exemption
homestead.text: 25% of the fair market value of a single family home and its land is exempt, on the first $1,000,000 of value (W.S. 39-11-105(a)(xlvi)). From tax year 2026 the owner must live in the home at least 8 months a year (active-duty military excepted). It cannot be combined with the long-term homeowner exemption on the same property.

otherRelief.name: Long-term homeowner exemption
otherRelief.text: Owners 65+ (or spouse) who have paid Wyoming residential property tax for 25 years or more: 50% of the fair market value of the primary residence exempt, on the first $3,000,000. Claim with the county assessor by March 1. This paragraph is repealed effective July 1, 2027.

otherRelief.name: Property Tax Refund Program
otherRelief.text: State refund program for qualifying homeowners, based on median household income and median property tax figures published by the Department of Revenue (2025 tables).

dueDates.text: Half of the tax is payable by November 10 and the other half by May 10 of the next year; paying the whole tax by December 31 avoids interest and penalty.

facts.text: Residential property is assessed at 9.5% of value: a $400,000 home has an assessed value of $38,000 before exemptions.
The 4% annual cap on assessed value of homes resets when the property is bought: the new owner is valued at full value the following year.
The 50% long-term homeowner exemption for seniors is scheduled to be repealed on July 1, 2027.
The first $75,000 of business personal property per owner in each county is exempt.
